chunks: 37 - The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله would, when he intended to enter the place of ablution, say: “O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the vile, impure, evil, corrupting Satan, the accursed. O Allah, remove harm from me and grant me refuge from Satan, the accursed.”
And when he had settled sitting for wudu (ablution), he would say: “O Allah, remove from me filth and harm, and make me among those who purify themselves.”
And when he strained to relieve himself, he would say: “O Allah, just as You fed it to me wholesome in well-being, then bring it out from me foul in well-being.”

key_terms.ٱلْمُتَوَضَّإِ: the place of ablution, here referring to the lavatory or washing place

ai.seo_question: What du'as did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله recite when entering the lavatory and preparing for wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith records supplications of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله connected to relieving oneself and preparing for wudu (ablution). It emphasizes seeking refuge from Shaytan, asking Allah for removal of harm and impurity, and maintaining bodily purity with gratitude for health.
